name: QUARTILE
description: QUARTILE returns the quartile (0th through 4th) of a dataset using the inclusive method. It is the legacy function, retained for compatibility.
tldr: Returns the specified quartile (0=min, 1, 2=median, 3, 4=max) of a dataset.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The range or array of numeric values.

parameters.name: quart
parameters.description: Which quartile to return: 0=minimum, 1=first, 2=median, 3=third, 4=maximum. An integer from 0 to 4.

basicExample.explanation: The median of 1..8 is the average of the 4th and 5th values: (4+5)/2 = 4.5.

advancedExamples.title: First quartile with interpolation
advancedExamples.description: Uses the inclusive method equivalent to PERCENTILE.INC with k = 0.25.

advancedExamples.title: Fourth quartile returns the maximum
advancedExamples.explanation: quart = 4 corresponds to the maximum, which is 8.

howItWorks: QUARTILE computes quartiles using the inclusive method, internally equivalent to PERCENTILE.INC(array, quart/4). It returns the minimum (quart 0), first quartile (quart 1), median (quart 2), third quartile (quart 3), or maximum (quart 4). Values are interpolated when the quartile position is fractional. quart must be an integer from 0 to 4, else #NUM!. Text and logical values are ignored.

howToSteps.name: Select the result cell
howToSteps.text: Click where you want the quartile.

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =QUARTILE(range, quart) with quart from 0 to 4.

limitations: quart must be an integer from 0 to 4; other values cause #NUM!.
May interpolate, so the result need not be an actual data value.
Ignores text and logical values in the array.

commonErrors.cause: quart is less than 0, greater than 4, or non-integer; or the array is empty.
commonErrors.fix: Use an integer quart in 0..4 and ensure the range has numbers.
Use QUARTILE.EXC only if the exclusive definition is required.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports QUARTILE with the same inclusive behavior as legacy Excel.

faq.question: Is QUARTILE the same as QUARTILE.INC?
faq.answer: Yes. QUARTILE is the legacy name for the inclusive method; QUARTILE.INC is the Excel 2010+ equivalent.

faq.question: What does quart = 2 return?
faq.answer: It returns the second quartile, which is the median of the dataset.

faq.question: Why do QUARTILE and QUARTILE.EXC give different answers?
faq.answer: QUARTILE (inclusive) uses rank 1 + k*(n-1) and allows the min/max; QUARTILE.EXC uses rank k*(n+1) and excludes the endpoints.
